title: Wayland+Vulkan: main loop freezes ~20 s at first frame after window returns from a hidden workspace (Mesa FIFO present thread blocks on buffer release; presentation schedule runs ahead by the hidden duration)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]

### System information

Arch Linux (kernel 7.1.6-arch1-1) - Wayland, Hyprland 0.56.2 (commit efb50993) - Vulkan (Forward+) - Intel UHD Graphics (CML GT2), Mesa 26.1.6, Vulkan API 1.4.354 - two monitors

### Issue description

A project window sitting on a workspace the user switches away from
(surface hidden / not composited) freezes the **entire main loop** for
up to 20.0 s at the moment the user switches back — no input
processing, no close handling, frozen picture (long stalls end with the
screen going black until the freeze breaks). Close requests and keys
pressed during the freeze are all processed in a burst when it ends.

Measured behavior (instrumented 1 Hz heartbeat + `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1`
protocol traces; many sessions over several days):

- The freeze length is capped at a hard **20.0 ± 0.3 s** (constant
  across absences of 40 s … 4 min; measured at that exact value in six
  separate sessions).
- Short absences freeze proportionally (e.g. ~4 s absence → ~4.3 s
  freeze).
- The app is completely healthy while hidden: the window suspend works
  (`Engine.get_frames_drawn()` is frozen the whole time, zero Wayland
  traffic beyond keepalives), the main loop iterates normally in
  low_processor mode.
- With `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1`, the freeze is visible on the wire as Mesa's
  `{mesa vk display queue}` thread going silent for **exactly 20.004 s
  between two consecutive `wl_surface.commit`s** while the main thread
  is blocked behind it (heartbeat silent, so likely in
  `vkAcquireNextImageKHR` waiting for a free swapchain image; an
  earlier gdb session of a related variant showed the block inside a
  `drm_syncobj_array_wait_timeout` ioctl — an explicit-sync release
  wait).
- Mesa's FIFO presentation schedule (`wp_commit_timer_v1.set_timestamp`
  targets) resumes after re-show with **stale pre-hide timestamps**,
  and then jumps forward by **exactly the hidden duration** (e.g. 59 s
  hidden → target jumps +59 s). Both facts are visible in the attached
  trace excerpts.
- A control scene in the same project that renders nothing shows the
  SAME stale-schedule commits and the SAME schedule jump on return, but
  drains them all in under 50 ms with no freeze. The difference appears
  to be swapchain buffer availability at drain time: the freezing run
  stalls after two commits (out of free images, waiting on a buffer
  release the compositor hasn't sent), the clean one drains six
  commits immediately.

What is ruled out by experiments (all measured):

1. Not XWayland: running the same project with `--display-driver x11`
   does not freeze. Native Wayland backend only.
2. Not the render loop or app-side rendering while hidden: freezes
   reproduce with the window suspend engaged and frames_drawn frozen
   throughout the absence.
3. Not vsync mode (`VSYNC_MAILBOX` unchanged) and not cured by
   recreating the swapchain right before the first draw after re-show
   (measured: recreation takes 16 ms, freeze unchanged).
4. Compositor-scripted workspace switches (`hyprctl dispatch`) do NOT
   reproduce — only real input-driven (keybind) switches do. The
   distinguishing observable: an input-driven switch plays the
   workspace slide animation and the window renders a few frames into
   the slide-out after focus loss, so it goes dark with presents in
   flight; a dispatch switch hides it instantly with none. (This is
   also why naive scripted reproduction attempts look clean.)
5. The freeze needs nontrivial scene content, and the trigger is
   narrower than any single property we could isolate. Reproduces
   100 % of the time: our game's GPU-heavy scenes (a stereogram
   renderer running continuously at ~31-33 fps: SubViewports feeding a
   per-frame RenderingDevice compute solve at 1920x1080). Never
   reproduces (all hand-tested with the same gesture): an empty scene
   in the same project; light scenes of the same game whose renderers
   sleep (poke-driven SubViewport UPDATE_ONCE); and seven synthetic
   minimal projects covering the suspects one by one and in
   combination — spinning rect (60 fps), TIME-shader rect, SubViewport
   + RD compute dispatch at 60 fps, heavy fragment shader at ~33 fps,
   and heavy-shader-inside-SubViewport + RD compute at ~16 fps. So
   neither continuous rendering, nor sub-60-fps GPU load, nor
   viewports, nor compute dispatches alone (or combined) suffice. We
   attach the last synthetic attempt as instrumentation and full
   `WAYLAND_DEBUG` traces of a freezing and a non-freezing run; we can
   run further instrumented sessions on request.
6. There are TWO manifestations, seen in back-to-back sessions of
   different scenes of the same game (1 Hz heartbeat with
   `Engine.get_frames_drawn()`):
   - **A — loop blocked**: heartbeat stops for exactly the freeze
     duration at the first frame after return; input and close queue
     behind it (most sessions).
   - **B — display withheld**: heartbeat and frames_drawn continue at
     full rate immediately after return and input works, but the
     visible picture stays frozen ~20 s (one session, same scene
     class). This matches the compositor honoring the stale/jumped
     `wp_commit_timer_v1` timestamps — frames are produced and
     committed but scheduled up to a minute into the future.

Working model: while the surface is hidden the FIFO present machinery's
schedule keeps advancing; on re-show the queued stale-schedule frames
must drain, and if the swapchain has no free images at that moment the
present thread blocks on an explicit-sync buffer release that the
compositor does not deliver until a ~20 s timeout elapses. The main
thread blocks behind it in acquire, freezing the game. Whether the fix
belongs in Godot (avoid presenting into the hide transition / re-sync
the schedule on resume), Mesa's Wayland WSI (clamp the schedule to now,
don't wait unbounded on release), or Hyprland (release buffers of
hidden surfaces promptly) is unclear to us — reporting here first since
the user impact is in Godot applications, with measurements attached.

Application-side mitigation we ship meanwhile (works, may help others):
on `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_FOCUS_OUT` disable the render loop and
raise the low-processor sleep (5 Hz, later 1 Hz); restore on focus-in.
Residual freeze ≈ 1 s per minute of absence.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Wayland session (observed on Hyprland 0.56.2), Vulkan renderer,
   `run/low_processor_usage_mode` on. Two-monitor setup not required.
2. Run a project with nontrivial 2D content (our reproducer is a game scene
   with SubViewports + per-frame RenderingDevice compute; the attached minimal project shows the instrumentation
   but does not freeze on our machine — see caveat 5 above).
3. Switch to another workspace **with a keyboard bind** (not a
   compositor IPC command), stay away ≥ 40 s, switch back.
4. Observe the heartbeat gap / frozen (then black) picture for 20 s;
   keys and close requests queue and burst through when it ends.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Attached: `wayland-return-stall-mrp.zip` — heartbeat + focus/close
instrumentation, low_processor mode, Wayland driver pinned
(`display_server/driver.linuxbsd="wayland"`; without it Godot picks
XWayland and nothing reproduces). NOTE: this MRP does not freeze on our
machine — content-dependence is part of the bug (see issue text). Full
`WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` traces of a freezing and a non-freezing session are
available on request (too large to attach).

[wayland-return-stall-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30901148/wayland-return-stall-mrp.zip)
